surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Wilson has a goal and two assists as the Capitals beat the Penguins
paras: Anthony Beauvillier got the scoring started for the Capitals just 23 seconds into the game, his 300th NHL point. Bryan Rust made it 1-1 for Pittsburgh 56 seconds later, in his first game of the season. Tom Wilson put the Capitals ahead for good midway through the first. It was a busy second period. Pierre-Luc Dubois stretched the lead to 3-1 early in the period. Alex Tuch made it 4-1 midway through the period, and that one stood up as the winner. Tommy Novak and Nick Robertson scored just under four minutes apart later in the period to cut Washington’s lead to 4-3, but that was as close as they got. Ryan Leonard stretched the lead to 5-3 on the power play early in the third. Wilson finished with a goal and two assists.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Logan Thompson made 27 saves for the Capitals, and Artūrs Šilovs stopped 22 of 27 at the other end. The Caps moved to 2-1-0 with a win in their home opener and took third place in the Metropolitan from the Penguins, who fell to 2-2-0.

items.text: Trevor van Riemsdyk played his first game back in Washington.
